processing: Ripe pu-erh pressed into a 357 g cake; the recipe itself is not publicly set out, but ripe tea from this area is typically Yunnan large-leaf sun-dried tea that is wet-piled and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea; factory ripe blends are generally not tied to a single picking.
appearance_dry: A 357 g round cake; expect the dark, reddish-brown leaf typical of Menghai ripe tea.
appearance_liquor: Typical of ripe pu-erh: deep red-brown.
appearance_wet: Typical of ripe pu-erh: soft, dark brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting notes for this recipe; ripe Menghai blends usually run smooth, earthy and sweet.

brewing.notes: General ripe pu-erh approach: one quick rinse, water near the boil, short early steeps.

vintage_note: Sold by production year as a 357 g cake. A 2005 special order made tippier than the standard blend has been sold, and a 2006 commemorative edition for the 50th anniversary of a Guangdong artists' association. Beyond that the release record is thin, and as with other ripe cakes, an older one is only as good as its storage.
description:
7576 is a numbered ripe cake from Fuhai Tea Factory in Menghai, a county better known abroad for its bigger neighbour, Menghai Tea Factory. The number works like the recipe codes used across the region, though this particular recipe is not publicly set out.

Assume only what is typical of its class: Yunnan large-leaf tea, wet-piled and pressed, here into a 357 g cake.

There are few tasting notes to go on, so brew it like other ripe Menghai tea and decide for yourself: quick rinse, water near the boil, short early steeps.

When buying, check the year, how it was stored, and whether it is a commemorative wrapper, which may affect price without saying anything about the tea.
history:
Fuhai began in 1983 as Menghai County's Xinghuo Tea Factory, staffed by managers and technicians from Menghai Tea Factory, and first made black tea. It was renamed Fuhai in 1998 to concentrate on pu-erh.

A 2005 special-order version of 7576, made tippier for a Guangzhou tea seller, and a 2006 commemorative cake are on record. When the recipe was first made is not documented.
